questions.q: What does "source-driven development" mean for a Salesforce project?
options: Local, version-controlled files are the source of truth, and the org is a deployment target
The org is always the source of truth and files are just a backup
It means writing only Apex code, never declarative configuration
It means Salesforce no longer requires a CLI at all
questions.explain: The lesson defines source-driven development as treating local, version-controlled project files as the source of truth, with the org as a deployment target.

questions.q: What is the current Salesforce CLI command, as confirmed in this lesson?
options: sfdx, the long-standing command that has never changed
salesforce-cli, a command that has never existed
force, the original 2010s-era command
sf, the current CLI shipped as the npm package @salesforce/cli -- sfdx was the previous major version
questions.explain: The lesson confirms the current CLI commands start with sf (package @salesforce/cli), with sfdx being the retired previous major version.

questions.q: What does the sf org login web command do?
options: Deletes an org permanently
Deploys all local metadata to production immediately
Opens a browser window to log in and links that org to the CLI under an alias
Generates a new Salesforce DX project folder
questions.explain: The lesson describes sf org login web as opening a browser login flow and linking the authenticated org to the CLI under an alias.

questions.q: What is the difference between sf project deploy start and sf project retrieve start?
options: They are two names for the exact same command
deploy start pushes local source into the org; retrieve start pulls org metadata back into local source
deploy start only works on scratch orgs, and retrieve start only works on production
retrieve start deletes metadata from the org
questions.explain: The lesson explains deploy start pushes local source into the org, while retrieve start pulls metadata from the org back into local source.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should never be committed to a Salesforce Git repository?
options: Real data, org credentials, auth URLs, and security tokens
Object and field definitions
Flow definitions and permission sets
The sfdx-project.json configuration file
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against committing real data, credentials, auth URLs, or security tokens, and notes the default .gitignore already excludes the local auth directories.
